subject: Partial routing degradation during EdgeMesh maintenance — apportionment request
messages:
From: Sara Wu <sara.wu@orionhealth.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: michael.torres@orionhealth.com
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Partial routing degradation observed this morning (prod) — request for SLA treatment

Hi Tessa,

We saw a repeated partial degradation impacting our production inference calls between 08:21 and 08:39 PDT this morning (roughly 18 minutes). For about half the affected requests clients returned 500s; our retries hit higher latencies and we saw increased error rates in our dashboards. We've attached a short incident log from our side (orion_incident_log_0819.txt) and our preliminary SLO impact calc (slo_calc_orion_0819.xlsx).

Orion's runbook points at routing/edge-level failures as a top cause; your status page showed an EdgeMesh maintenance notice overlapping the window: the maintenance notice listed a planned routing update for 08:00–08:30 PDT. Can you confirm whether this counts as a Redwood maintenance window or a third-party exception? If it's excluded, please explain how the partial-degrade apportionment will be done — we need the breakdown for our internal audit and to decide whether to pursue the full 100% credit.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Wu
Head of Platform Ops — Orion Health

Hi Sara — sorry you hit this. Thanks for the packet and the SLO calc. I'm looping in Marissa from SRE to examine the telemetry and Sean from Billing to track the credit side.

Initial notes:
- Our incident timeline shows elevated 5xx rates in the same window.
- EdgeMesh posted a maintenance advisory with a 08:00–08:30 PDT target; our controller routed ~12% of Orion traffic over an alternate path during the window but there was observable tail error amplification.

Marissa, can you confirm whether this should be treated as Redwood maintenance (eligible for maintenance exclusion) vs a third-party outage (apportionment)? If apportionment, please propose the percentage to attribute to Redwood vs EdgeMesh. Sean, please standby for any billing action pending the technical assessment.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Sara Wu <sara.wu@orionhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 09:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Partial routing degradation observed this morning (prod) — technical apportionment proposal

Hi team,

We've pulled the traces and edge logs. Summary below (high level):

Timeline (PDT):
- 08:00 — EdgeMesh scheduled rolling routing update (public notice attached edgemesh-maintenance-notice.pdf).
- 08:18–08:39 — Elevated 5xx rates for Orion-specific logical paths; peak at 08:24.

Findings:
- The maintenance was performed by EdgeMesh, but the rollout had a misconfigured route priority for our Orion tenant which caused ~38% of Orion's traffic to be sent to a legacy route without KV cache warming.
- Redwood's serving layer detected degraded responses and attempted automatic path-fanout to alternate regions at 08:22; however, because KV cache state is per-path, those failovers experienced cold-cache penalties and some requests still returned 500s until KV warmed.
- Our controller shows ~62% of the observed errors were correlated with the legacy route packets; ~38% correlated with downstream timeout propagation during the failover window.

Recommendation for apportionment:
- Treat EdgeMesh maintenance as a third-party maintenance (not Redwood-scheduled). EdgeMesh's operational mistake (mis-prioritized rollout) makes them primarily responsible for the root cause.
- Apportionment proposal for the 18-minute window: 70% third-party (EdgeMesh), 30% Redwood. Rationale: the majority of routing disruption is due to EdgeMesh rollout, but Redwood's failover mechanics and cold-cache impact increased customer-facing error exposure.

We can provide the raw correlation report and the per-minute error breakdown (CSV). If Orion disputes the 70/30 split, we'll accept mediation and can run a joint replay using the request IDs included in orion_incident_log_0819.txt.

Marissa Cole
Senior SRE — Redwood Inference
attachments: edgemesh-maintenance-notice.pdf
From: Sara Wu <sara.wu@orionhealth.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, michael.torres@orionhealth.com
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Partial routing degradation observed this morning (prod) — technical apportionment proposal

Tessa / Marissa — thanks for the breakdown. We appreciate the quick triage. A couple of points from Orion:

- From our perspective the failover did not behave as expected; our runbook includes a multi-region fanout that should have absorbed this type of routing hiccup. The reason it didn't appears to be the cold-KV behavior you described, which we believe is an architectural constraint of Redwood's routing. That leans responsibility back toward Redwood.
- For contract purposes we need an itemized SLO invoice showing the applied credit calculation and the applied apportionment math.

Request: please provide the per-minute error correlation CSV, the exact apportionment formula (so we can replicate), and a draft credit note for the 30% Redwood responsibility. If you will not accept 50/50, include the justification data so our procurement team can review.

We'd like to keep this between ops teams; procurement and legal will get involved if we can't reconcile.

Regards,
Sara
From: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Sara Wu <sara.wu@orionhealth.com>, tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2026 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Partial routing degradation observed this morning (prod) — credit draft attached

Hi Sara — thanks for the note. Attached is a draft credit note that applies a 30% service credit for the 18-minute impacted window per Marissa's apportionment (slo-based calculation included). The draft shows:

- Calculation inputs: total impacted minutes, Orion's contract monthly SLO period, and Redwood's unit credit rate (per SLA).
- Applied apportionment: 30% Redwood / 70% third-party (EdgeMesh).
- Net credit: a pro-rated credit equal to 30% of the computed outage impact for the 18 minutes, applied against Orion's billing period.

If Orion wants to propose 50/50, we are open to mediation. Otherwise, once you confirm acceptance we will issue a formal credit memo and post to your account billing.

Sean Gallagher
Billing Operations — Redwood Inference
attachments: draft_credit_orion_0819.pdf
